Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

# Heirloom: build brief

**For the coding agent working in the `heirloom/` repo. This is the spec; build exactly this.**
Everything here is public information or our own design.

## 1. What we're building

**Heirloom is an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched.** It backports each new upstream security fix to the old release lines that Linux distributions still ship. It proves which lines are actually vulnerable, adapts and verifies the fix, and asks a person only when it can't prove something.

### First target: Django 4.2
- Django 4.2 reached end of extended support on 2026-04-07 (last release 4.2.30). Upstream has **deleted the `stable/4.2.x` branch**; the line now lives only in tags. Its last release is tag `4.2.30` = `3396992e83` (2026-04-07).
- Distros still ship it: Debian 13 "trixie" has `python-django 3:4.2.28-0+deb13u2`, and Ubuntu 24.04 "noble" has `3:4.2.11-1ubuntu1.18`. Distro security teams hand-backport every new Django CVE to 4.2.
- Since EOL, 19 Django CVEs were fixed upstream on 6.1/6.0/5.2 only. None has a 4.2 patch:
  - 2026-05-05: CVE-2026-5766, 35192, 6907
  - 2026-06-03: CVE-2026-6873, 7666, 8404, 35193, 48587
  - 2026-07-07: CVE-2026-48588, 53877, 53878
  - 2026-08-04: CVE-2026-15307, 15337, 15830, 15920
  - 2026-10-06: CVE-2026-77050, 84429, 87890, 87975
- The authoritative list (with per-branch commit links) is `docs/releases/security.txt` on django/django `main`.

### The user
A distro or extended-support security engineer. Today they read each advisory, find the fix, figure out whether 4.2 is even affected, port the patch through 3+ years of divergence, and test it.

### The task, end to end and unattended
"Bring Django 4.2 current on security." For every CVE:
1. locate the upstream fix;
2. build a probe test;
3. **calibrate** it;
4. decide whether 4.2 is affected;
5. adapt the fix;
6. verify fail-before/pass-after;
7. check behaviour against upstream;
8. publish a PR on our public fork;
9. ask a human only when evidence runs out.

It watches the security archive and starts on new advisories automatically.

### Design principle
- **Facts are decided by executed evidence, never by the model.** Is the line vulnerable? Does the fix work? Calibrated tests decide.
- **Mechanics are automated:** adapting code through divergence, recovering a broken environment, retries.
- **Choices are asked once and remembered:** something it can't prove in this environment, or an adapted fix that behaves differently from upstream's.
- **Frequent escalation is a failure mode too.** Report the escalation rate next to every score.

### Honesty rules (non-negotiable)
- Every number in README/docs comes from a run artifact (`evals/results*.json`).
- Patches are labelled "candidate backport — not an official Django release".
- Never claim NOT-AFFECTED without the calibration gates below. When unsure, say UNPROVEN.
- No fabricated results. No secrets in code, logs, commits or transcripts (keys live only in `.env`, which is gitignored).

## 2. Repo layout
```
heirloom/                       (public, MIT)
  pyproject.toml                (uv; python>=3.12)
  heirloom/
    cli.py                      Typer: campaign | cve | backtest | resume | watch | report | serve
    config.py                   settings from env (.env via python-dotenv)
    ledger.py                   SQLite effects ledger + state machine
    sources/django_security.py  parse security.txt → CVE → {branch: sha}, date, title
    git_ops.py                  worktrees, sanitized repos, diffs, blame, ancestry
    pipeline/{locate,probe,calibrate,presence,adapt,verify,behaviour,decide,publish}.py
......
## 5. Sponsor integrations (in the loop)

### neatlogs (agent observability)
- `pip install "neatlogs[litellm]"`. Call `neatlogs.init(api_key=env NEATLOGS_API_KEY, workflow_name="heirloom", instrumentations=["litellm"], tags=[...])` **before importing litellm**, and `neatlogs.flush(); neatlogs.shutdown()` on exit.
- **Sessions:** `with neatlogs.identify(session_id=f"campaign-{run}")` for the campaign. Each CVE gets `identify(session_id=f"cve-{id}-{run}", parent_session_id=f"campaign-{run}")`.
- **Spans:** `with neatlogs.trace("<stage>", kind="AGENT|TOOL|GUARDRAIL") as span: span.set_attribute(...)`.
  - Always set (explicit values, never missing): `heirloom.cve`, `heirloom.line`, `heirloom.stage`, `heirloom.verdict`, `heirloom.calibrated`, `heirloom.reach`, `heirloom.reason`, `heirloom.tests_edited_after_red`, `heirloom.claims_unlinked`, `heirloom.cost_usd`, `heirloom.claim_id`.
  - Wrap each `claude -p` run in an AGENT span carrying its `total_cost_usd`, `session_id` and checkpoint id (headless calls bypass the LiteLLM instrumentation).
- **Detections** (Public API `https://app.neatlogs.com/api/v1/public`, headers `Authorization: Bearer $NEATLOGS_SERVICE_TOKEN`, `x-project-id: $NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID`, `idempotency-key`).
  - Create **conditional** detections on span attributes **before the v1 baseline runs**: `not_affected_without_calibration`, `fix_applied_where_probe_passed`, `probe_never_reached_region`, `claim_without_span`, `test_edited_after_red`.
  - Read `GET /detections/{id}/hits` and `/trends?granularity=hour` for the before/after chart. Check the conditional config syntax with `neatlogs schema search` or the docs first.
  - Backfill is not available on our tier; don't depend on it.
- **MCP:** the agent may call `search_traces` / `get_trace_context` (`https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp`, Bearer project key) to look up past failures of the same class (env build, flaky module) and reuse the recovery.

### Entire (agent sessions as git checkpoints)
- **Build time:** this repo has `entire enable --agent claude-code`. Use Entire deliberately and record the outputs in `hackathon.md`:
  - `entire status`, `entire checkpoint list`, `entire checkpoint explain <id>`;
  - `entire graph impact` (after `entire plugin install graph`);
  - `entire review` on a branch;
  - `entire recap`.
- **Runtime:** for each fork worktree, run `entire enable --agent claude-code --yes --local --telemetry=false`. Add `"commit_linking": "always"` to `.entire/settings.local.json`, and add `.claude/` and `.entire/` to `.git/info/exclude`.
  - After the orchestrator commits, check `git log -1 --format=%B | grep '^Entire-Checkpoint:'` and record the checkpoint id. Push the checkpoint refs with the branch. The PR links the checkpoint.
  - If trailers don't appear in headless mode, the fallback is an Agent Integration Protocol plugin `entire-agent-heirloom` (subcommands: info, detect, get-session-id, get-session-dir, resolve-session-file, read-session, write-session, read-transcript, chunk-transcript, reassemble-transcript, format-resume-command). Only if time allows.

### cfo.ai (business plan)
Done through the cfo.ai MCP in a session with that MCP connected. Inputs must be **measured**: cost per CVE from neatlogs/ledger, EC2 $/hour, human minutes per escalation.
- **Pricing hypotheses:** per verified backport, and a per-package-line monthly subscription for distro/ELTS teams.
- Scenarios base/bear/bull, a runway view, and a shared Page.
- Export a summary to `docs/business-plan.md` with the Page link.

## 6. Evals (real ground truth; numbers only from runs)
.....
### 10.7 Outreach drafts (never filed by the agent; the human files each one)
Write drafts to `docs/outreach/`, each built only from confirmed artifacts:
- `ubuntu-cve-2026-87890.md`: Launchpad bug text for python-django (noble). Contents: facts with links, calibrated probe results, candidate patch.
- `debian-cve-2026-53878.md`: security-tracker correction proposal with the provenance proof.
- `neatlogs-pii-dlq.md`: issue with a minimal repro of large-attribute spans stalling at pii_redaction.
- `entire-empty-repo-session.md`: issue: a session started before the first commit is never tracked ("failed to get HEAD").

**Required wording for the Ubuntu draft:** "noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path that upstream closed as CVE-2026-87890; our calibrated probe shows it." No exploitability claim. No jammy claim unless a 3.2 line was actually run.

## 11. Day-2 evening fixes (2026-10-11 16:00 UTC; OVERRIDES earlier sections)
- **Build sessions:** B1–B3 all ran in one old conversation (f5117257…). Entire tracked it only partly; its commits have no trailers, so it was recovered with `entire session attach` (checkpoints 01M4M7HF…, 01M4MDN1…, 01M4NVG1…). **Every session from B4 on must be a NEW conversation**, and its id must differ from f5117257.
- **Cost accounting:**
  - Recorded costs were about half of what the gateway billed. Use the provider-reported cost: OpenRouter's `usage.cost` (request `usage: {"include": true}`) and `claude -p` JSON `total_cost_usd`.
  - Reconcile against LiteLLM `/key/info` spend deltas where available.
  - Mark anything else `cost_estimated=true`. README/plan figures are lower bounds unless provider-reported.
- **Coverage for C3 reach:** run coverage with `concurrency = thread` (plus `multiprocessing` if used), so ASGI and threaded code paths count. Re-run only the CVE-2026-3902 backtest pair afterwards.
- **neatlogs detections without custom-attribute syntax:**
  - The pipeline emits a zero-work child span named `heirloom.flag.<predicate>` whenever a local predicate fires. The five predicates are: not_affected_without_calibration, fix_applied_where_probe_passed, probe_never_reached_region, claim_without_span, test_edited_after_red.
  - Each detection uses `runOn: {frequency: "span_name", span_names: ["heirloom.flag.<predicate>"]}` with a built-in field condition known to match (e.g. `latency_ms >= 0`).
  - Hits and trends then come from neatlogs. The ledger keeps the same predicates locally as the source of truth.
  - If the user supplies the dashboard's custom-attribute field syntax, switch the condition to the attribute. Otherwise keep the flag spans.
- **Matrix:** after the campaign gives the 13 missing CVEs a calibrated probe, re-run the matrix over 4.2.30, debian-trixie and ubuntu-noble.
Shell cwd was reset to /home/ubuntu/heirloom
```

## cfoai
# cfo.ai MCP

You are connected to **cfo.ai** — an AI-native financial planning workspace. This MCP exposes Ari's public product tools for you to call directly. You can both **read** a company's financial model and **change** it: create and edit scenarios, pages, table blocks, Canvas blocks, formulas, variables, dimensions, and data ingestion.

Model-editing tools change the live model immediately and record reversible changes in its
changelog. Connections, access changes, and outbound actions have effects outside model undo. Build from saved data, research, supplied numbers, estimates, hypotheses, or invented
assumptions. Clearly label uncited inputs and their basis in the model and handoff. Create missing
model objects and editable inputs as part of the work. A missing source citation does not block modeling.

## Read the reference before you build

cfo.ai has its own modeling method, described under "How a table shows the model" below: how tables show variables, dimensions, and fields, how a reference reads from the cell it sits in, and how a table's rows and columns are built. `inspect_skills` owns the built-in and workspace skill catalog. Use its `list` block to find a skill and its `instructions` block to read it.

Read `build-model` before creating or changing model logic, variables, dimensions, or saved tables;
`build-visualizations` before adding a Canvas block; and `import-model` before rebuilding a model
from a workbook or export. Each manual contains its complete reference in `SKILL.md`.

Workspace skills hold company-specific playbooks. Read the relevant saved guidance before substantial work.

## Calling convention

- A multi-action tool selects one operation with the block named for that action; single-purpose tools use their fields directly. Supply only fields supported inside the selected block. An `inspect_*` tool reads saved product state; an `edit_*` tool changes it.
- `target` identifies an existing object where the operation needs one, including the destination of a new block. Creation fields describe the new object: use the selected operation's `name`, `title`, `source`, or other published fields. On an update, `name` gives the selected object's new name.
- Supply `org_id` when selecting a workspace by ID or slug. If you belong to exactly one workspace, the server selects it automatically. Use `list_orgs` when the correct workspace is unclear.
- Tools accept an optional `_context` object — `{ layerId, pageId, timeZone, utcOffset }` — that mirrors the in-app editing context. Supply `layerId` for the active scenario, `pageId` for the current page, and `timeZone` or `utcOffset` when relative dates matter. Identify existing objects by readable names or references returned by an inspection.
- Model object selectors accept names, returned `Name#hex` disambiguators, or IDs unless the field states a narrower contract. A returned `Name#a1b` carries a prefix of the object's identity, at least three hex digits and unique among every object of its kind when the result was written; later creates can lengthen it, so a reference from an older result resolves while it stays unique, and a fresh inspection carries the current spelling. Ambiguous or unknown names return candidates when available. Each tool defines singular or plural targets, omitted/empty/null input behavior, and scenario defaults.
- Reuse pagination cursors unchanged with the same tool, action, target, filters, and snapshot. Each cursor field names the returned value to use and any special empty-string behavior.
- A saved table is created or reshaped with its complete visible `rows` and `columns`. A dimension path may use a bounded member `filter`, an ancestor `when` condition, or independent sibling `branches`. Inspection returns the same saved shape under `layout.rows` and `layout.columns`. Updates use `row_updates`, `column_updates`, and `cell_updates`. An `add_dimension_items` entry places a planned member `under` an existing inspected parent.
- A Canvas block reads model values through named `datasets`. Each dataset declares the same visible sh… [truncated]

def _notes(ctx: Ctx, d: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    notes = [n for n in (ctx.note, d.get("decide", {}).get("note")) if n]
    prec = (d.get("decide") or {}).get("precedent")
    if prec:
        notes.append(
            f"Decision `{d['decide']['decision']}` applies stored precedent "
            f"**{prec['id']}** ({prec['issue']})."
        )

    cve: str

    run_id: str
    verdict: str = "PENDING"
    reason: str = "NONE"

    checkpoint: str = ""
    cost_usd: float = 0.0
    message: str = ""

def new_run_id() -> str:
    return time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime()) + "-" + secrets.token_hex(2)


@contextmanager
def lock(path: Path) -> Iterator[None]:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("w") as fh:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except BlockingIOError:
            raise ConcurrentRunError(f"another heirloom process holds {path}") from None
        fh.write(str(os.getpid()))

        try:

def _probe_error(detail: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "verdict": "UNPROVEN",
        "reason": "PROBE_ERROR",
        "calibrated": False,
        "detail": detail,
        "gates": {},
    }


def calibrated_probe(ledger: Ledger, cve: str, line: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """The discriminating probe of a finished run of (cve, line), for reuse on other lines.

    Reuse needs C1 (FAIL on U⁻, PASS on U⁺, stable ids); C2/C3/C4 are line-specific
    and are re-checked on the new line by on_line().
    """
    rows = [r for r in ledger.stages(cve, line) if r.status == "done"]
    pres = [
        r
        for r in rows
        if r.key.stage == "presence"
        and ((r.output or {}).get("gates", {}).get("C1") or {}).get("ok")
    ]
    probes = [r for r in rows if r.key.stage == "probe" and r.output]
    if not pres or not probes:

    return max(probes, key=lambda r: r.key.attempt).output

    return lambda span: probe_

    loc = locate.run(ctx)
    if any(f.startswith("django/contrib/gis/") for f in loc["fix_files"]):
        ctx.settings_module = "test_postgis"  # GIS fixes run against the PostGIS container
    c0 = calibrate.run_c0(ctx, loc)

    feedback: str | None = None
    pr_: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    cal: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    pres = _probe_error("no probe")
    budget_hit = ""  # a per-CVE or overflow cap stopped a model call
    # Reuse mode (other lines, fixed twins, matrix): no porter call and no retries;
    # an ERROR on the new line is UNPROVEN(PROBE_ERROR) by the verdict table.
    models = ctx.s.porter_models()
    for attempt in range(1 if reuse_probe else 3):  # first probe + up to 2 porter retries

            model = models[min(attempt, len(models) - 1)]
            if reuse_probe is not None:

                inputs = {"reuse": reuse_probe["sha"], "record": 3}
                pr_ = ctx.stage("probe", inputs, _given(reuse_probe))
            else:
                pr_ = probe.run(ctx, loc, c0, feedback, model=model)
        except (StageFailed, probe.LeakageError) as exc:
            pres = _probe_error(str(exc))
            if isinstance(exc, StageFailed) and reuse_probe is None and model != models[-1]:

                feedback = f"Your previous probes were rejected before running: {exc}"
                continue

        except BudgetExceeded as exc:
            budget_hit = str(exc)
            if cal is None:  # no calibrated probe at all
                pres = {**_probe_error(budget_hit), "reason": "BUDGET"}
            break
        cal = calibrate.run(ctx, loc, pr_)
        pres = calibrate.run_presence(ctx, cal)
        if not cal.get("feedback"):
            break
        feedback = cal["feedback"]

ad: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ver: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    beh: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    if pres["verdict"] == "AFFECTED" and pr_ is not None and cal is not None:
        hint: str | None = None
        for _ in range(3):  # ADAPT at most 3×, VERIFY's failure as the hint
            try:
                ad = adapt.run(ctx, loc, pr_, cal, hint)
            except (StageFailed, EntireError) as exc:
                hint, ad = str(exc), None
                continue
            except BudgetExceeded as exc:
                budget_hit, ad = str(exc), None
                break
            ver = verify.run(ctx, loc, pr_, cal, ad)
            if ver["ok"]:
                break
            changed = verify.upstream_test_change(ver, loc)
            if changed:
                # Only 4.2's versions of tests upstream rewrote fail: re-adapting cannot
                # help without diverging from upstream. A human chooses (DECIDE).
                ver = {**ver, "upstream_test_change": changed}
                break
            hint = ver["hint"]
        if ad is not None and ver is not None and ver["ok"]:
            beh = behaviour.run(ctx, loc, pr_, ad)

    if budget_hit and not (ver is not None and ver["ok"]) and pres["verdict"] == "AFFECTED":
        # Calibrated AFFECTED, but no verified fix within the cap: evidence, not a fix.
        pres = {
            **pres,
            "verdict": "UNPROVEN",
            "reason": "BUDGET",
            "detail": f"AFFECTED by the calibrated probe; no verified fix: {budget_hit}",
        }
    dec = decide.run(ctx, pres, ver, beh)
    if dec["decision"] == "match-upstream" and ad is not None and pr_ is not None and cal:
        # The stored answer: make 4.2 behave exactly like upstream, then verify again.
        hint = "Match upstream's observable behaviour exactly; these differ:\n" + "\n".join(
            decide._diffs(beh, None)
        )
        ad2 = adapt.run(ctx, loc, pr_, cal, hint)
        ver2 = verify.run(ctx, loc, pr_, cal, ad2)
        beh2 = behaviour.run(ctx, loc, pr_, ad2) if ver2["ok"] else None
        if ver2["ok"] and beh2 is not None and beh2["same"]:
            ad, ver, beh = ad2, ver2, beh2
            dec = {**dec, "decision": "publish-fix", "matched_upstream": True}
        else:
            dec = {**dec, "decision": "publish-evidence", "matched_upstream": False}
    adopted: list[str] = []
    if dec["decision"] == "adopt-upstream-tests" and ad is not None and pr_ is not None and cal:
        # The stored answer: carry upstream's own test changes, verify, then decide again.
        ver2 = verify.adopt_upstream_tests(ctx, loc, pr_, cal, ad, ver or {})
        if ver2["ok"]:
            ver, adopted = ver2, list(ver2["adopted_tests"])
            beh = behaviour.run(ctx, loc, pr_, ad)
            prec = dec.get("precedent")
            dec = decide.run(ctx, pres, ver, beh)
            if dec["decision"] == "publish-fix":
                dec = {
                    **dec,
                    "precedent": prec,
                    "note": f"Per precedent {(prec or {}).get('id', '?')}, this backport also "
                    "carries upstream's own changes to "
                    + ", ".join(f"`{f}`" for f in adopted)
                    + ", because the fix deliberately changes what those 4.2 tests asserted.",
                }
        else:
            dec = {**dec, "decision": "publish-evidence", "adopt_failed": ver2.get("hint")}
    base = Result(
        status="",
        cve=ctx.cve,
        line=ctx.line,
        run_id=ctx.run_id,
        verdict=pres["verdict"],
        reason=str(pres["reason"] or "NONE"),
        decision=str(dec["decision"]),
        escalated=bool(dec.get("asked") or dec.get("escalated")),
    )
    if not ctx.spec.publish:
        base.status = "evaluated"
        base.message = f"{ctx.spec.kind} line: decision {dec['decision']}; nothing published"
        if ad is not None and ver is not None:
            base.message += f"; fix verified={ver['ok']}"
        return base
    if dec["decision"] == "waiting_human":
        base.status, base.message = "waiting_human", f"question: {dec.get('issue', '')}"
        base.issue_url = str(dec.get("issue", ""))
        return base
    outputs: dict[str, Any] = {
        "locate": loc,
        "c0": c0,
        "probe": pr_,
        "calibrate": cal,
        "presence": pres,
        "adapt": ad,
        "verify": ver,
        "behaviour": beh,
        "decide": dec,
    }
    if dec["decision"] == "skip":
        base.status, base.message = "skipped", "decision skip (stored precedent)"
        return base
    publish_fix = dec["decision"] in ("publish-fix", "accept-difference")
    if not publish_fix or ad is None or pr_ is None or ver is None or not ver["ok"]:
        ev = publish.evidence(ctx, outputs)
        base.status, base.issue_url = "evidence", str(ev["url"])
        return base

    committed = publish.commit(ctx, loc, pr_, pres, ad["patch_sha"], adopted=adopted)
    pushed = publish.push(ctx, committed)
    art = publish.artifacts(ctx, {"remote_sha": pushed["remote_sha"]})
    subject = publish._message(ctx, loc, pres).splitlines()[0]
    outputs.update(commit=committed, push=pushed, commit_subject=subject)
    pr_out = publish.pr(ctx, outputs, art)
    base.status = "published"
    base.pr_url = pr_out["url"]
    base.checkpoint = committed.get("checkpoint") or ""
    return base


def execute(
    s: Settings,
    cve: str,
    spec: LineSpec,
    run_id: str | None = None,
    *,
    reuse_probe: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    campaign_id: str | None = None,
    archive_ref: str = "origin/main",
    done_fixes: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    note: str = "",
) -> Result:
    line = spec.name
    with lock(s.work / "locks" / f"{cve}-{line}.lock"):
        ledger = Ledger(s.ledger_path)
        if run_id is None:
            latest = ledger.latest_run(cve, line)
            unfinished = latest is not None and latest["status"] not in ("done", "waiting_human")
            run_id = latest["run_id"] if latest is not None and unfinished else new_run_id()
        ledger.start_run(run_id, cve, line, json.dumps(spec.to_json()))
        campaign = campaign_id or f"single-{run_id}"
        tel = Telemetry()
        tel.init(
            s.neatlogs_api_key,
            tags=["heirloom", f"campaign-{campaign}", f"run-{run_id}", cve, f"line-{line}"],
        )
        ctx = Ctx(s, ledger, tel, spec, cve, line, run_id, campaign_id=campaign)
        ctx.archive_ref, ctx.done_fixes, ctx.note = archive_ref, done_fixes, note
        status = "failed"
        try:
            with tel.cve_root(cve, line, run_id, campaign), guard.publishing(spec):
                result = pipeline(ctx, reuse_probe)
            done = ("published", "no_fix", "evaluated", "evidence", "skipped")
            status = "done" if result.status in done else result.status
            result.cost_usd = ledger.cost_total(cve, line)
            return result
        except (PausedForReconcile, Unresolvable) as exc:
            status = "paused"
            return Result(
                "paused", cve, line, run_id, ctx.verdict, ctx.reason, message=str(exc),
                cost_usd=ledger.cost_total(cve, line),

            "detail": f"AFFECTED by the calibrated probe; no verified fix: {budget_hit}",

    dec = decide.run(ctx, pres, ver, beh)

        if ver2["ok"] and beh2 is not None and beh2["same"]:
            ad, ver, beh = ad2, ver2, beh2
            dec = {**dec, "decision": "publish-fix", "matched_upstream": True}
        else:
            dec = {**dec, "decision": "publish-evidence", "matched_upstream": False}
    adopted: list[str] = []
    if dec["decision"] == "adopt-upstream-tests" and ad is not None and pr_ is not None and cal:
        # The stored answer: carry upstream's own test changes, verify, then decide again.
        ver2 = verify.adopt_upstream_tests(ctx, loc, pr_, cal, ad, ver or {})
        if ver2["ok"]:
            ver, adopted = ver2, list(ver2["adopted_tests"])
            beh = behaviour.run(ctx, loc, pr_, ad)

            dec = decide.run(ctx, pres, ver, beh)

        cve=ctx.cve,
        line=ctx.line,
        run_id=ctx.run_id,
        verdict=pres["verdict"],
        reason=str(pres["reason"] or "NONE"),
        decision=str(dec["decision"]),
        escalated=bool(dec.get("asked") or dec.get("escalated")),

        base.issue_url = str(dec.get("issue", ""))
        return base
    outputs: dict[str, Any] = {
        "locate": loc,
        "c0": c0,
        "probe": pr_,
        "calibrate": cal,
        "presence": pres,
        "adapt": ad,
        "verify": ver,
        "behaviour": beh,
        "decide": dec,
    }
    if dec["decision"] == "skip":
        base.status, base.message = "skipped", "decision skip (stored precedent)"
        return base

    art = publish.artifacts(ctx, {"remote_sha": pushed["remote_sha"]})

def execute(
    s: Settings,
    cve: str,
    spec: LineSpec,
    run_id: str | None = None,
    *,
    reuse_probe: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    campaign_id: str | None = None,
    archive_ref: str = "origin/main",
    done_fixes: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    note: str = "",
) -> Result:
    line = spec.name
    with lock(s.work / "locks" / f"{cve}-{line}.lock"):
        ledger = Ledger(s.ledger_path)
        if run_id is None:
            latest = ledger.latest_run(cve, line)
            unfinished = latest is not None and latest["status"] not in ("done", "waiting_human")
            run_id = latest["run_id"] if latest is not None and unfinished else new_run_id()
        ledger.start_run(run_id, cve, line, json.dumps(spec.to_json()))
        campaign = campaign_id or f"single-{run_id}"
        tel = Telemetry()
        tel.init(
            s.neatlogs_api_key,
            tags=["heirloom", f"campaign-{campaign}", f"run-{run_id}", cve, f"line-{line}"],
        )
        ctx = Ctx(s, ledger, tel, spec, cve, line, run_id, campaign_id=campaign)
        ctx.archive_ref, ctx.done_fixes, ctx.note = archive_ref, done_fixes, note
        status = "failed"
        try:
            with tel.cve_root(cve, line, run_id, campaign), guard.publishing(spec):
                result = pipeline(ctx, reuse_probe)
            done = ("published", "no_fix", "evaluated", "evidence", "skipped")
            status = "done" if result.status in done else result.status
            result.cost_usd = ledger.cost_total(cve, line)
            return result
        except (PausedForReconcile, Unresolvable) as exc:
            status = "paused"
            return Result(
                "paused", cve, line, run_id, ctx.verdict, ctx.reason, message=str(exc),
                cost_usd=ledger.cost_total(cve, line),
            )  # fmt: skip
        finally:
            ledger.finish_run(run_id, status)
            tel.shutdown()
            ledger.close()

@app.command()
def campaign(
    line: str = "4.2",
    replay: bool = typer.Option(False, help="Replay the security archive commit by commit."),
    workers: int = typer.Option(2, help="Parallel worker processes."),
    cap: float = typer.Option(18.0, help="Overflow USD this campaign may spend (provider cost)."),
    campaign_id: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--id", help="Continue this campaign."),
    cont: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--continue", help="Poll answers, then re-queue waiting/blocked events."
    ),
    plan_only: bool = typer.Option(False, help="Write the plan and stop."),
    requeue: list[str] | None = typer.Option(
        None, help="With --continue: also re-run these CVEs' events (after a harness fix)."
    ),
) -> None:
    """E2: every post-EOL advisory on a line; one PR or evidence issue per CVE."""
    import time

    from heirloom import answers
    from heirloom import campaign as cmp

    if not replay:
        raise typer.BadParameter("only --replay campaigns exist (BUILD-BRIEF §10.5)")
    if line not in LINES or not LINES[line].publish:
        raise typer.BadParameter(f"{line!r} is not a publishing line")
    s = config.load()
    path = cmp.state_path(s, campaign_id) if campaign_id else None
    if path is None or not path.exists():
        path = cmp.create(s, line, cap, campaign_id)
        typer.echo(f"planned {path}")
    if cont:
        for a in answers.poll(s):
            typer.echo(f"answer {a.option} on {a.issue} -> precedent {a.precedent}")
        typer.echo(f"re-queued: {cmp.reopen(path, tuple(requeue or ()))}")
    state = json.loads(path.read_text())
    for ev in state["events"]:
        deps = ",".join(ev.get("depends_on") or []) or "-"
        typer.echo(f"  {ev['id']:34} {ev['kind']:8} deps={deps:16} {ev['status']}")
    if plan_only:
        return
    procs = cmp.spawn_workers(path, workers, s.work / cmp.STATE_DIR / state["id"])
    while any(p.poll() is None for p in procs):
        time.sleep(20)
    out = cmp.results(s, path)
    (s.root / "evals" / "results_live.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2) + "\n")
    typer.echo(json.dumps(out["summary"], indent=1))
    for q in out["summary"]["questions"]:
        typer.echo(f"QUESTION (answer with /heirloom answer <option>): {q}")

    """Record (and refuse) any subprocess a guarded writer might start."""
    calls: list[list[str]] = []

    def fake_run(cmd: list[str], *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        calls.append(list(cmd))

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", fake_run)

    body = tmp_path / "body.md"
